pr_comments: What's the use case for this? I wouldn't think these would be rotated automatically.
If you use hashicorp vault, as described in the issue, they would be rotated.

In particular, https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/agent/index.html with a file sink.

Note that in particular, vault and consul are from the same company so the chances are high that you use both.

Hmm, can those actually be tied together? If this were possible and common I'd expect to be able to find a guide on how to do it, which I can't.

It also looks like Consul supports standard bearer tokens now, so we should check when that happened and see if we can switch.

they support both but I decided to use X-Consul-Token as this is what the native go client uses.

here is the documentation to have vault creating short term rotating consul tokens:

https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/secrets/consul/
We already have code to deal with normal bearer tokens though.
Ok I will normalize on normal bearer
@roidelapluie Could I help you to finalize this issue ?

issue_context.title: feature: Support loading file for Consul Token
issue_context.body:
## Proposal

I use vault as a secret storage solution and I think it could be useful to support loading the consul token from a file like the `bearer_token_file`. For exemple, the Marathon SD already support it.

What do you think ?
If you like it, I could start working on a PR.

Thanks
comments:
The issue is that the upstream consul library never re-reads the file again. Would that still suit your need?

https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/blob/c91d0fa2c9629d74e5fe70e4acf9351f5c22858d/api/api.go#L305
That's not in line with how we do such files elsewhere, and I can see that causing confusion.

We went through this issue in our bug scrub and this might be possible by switching to a httpTransport passed to the consul client.

@roidelapluie Could you investigate the issue further, and tag it appropriately? As you've looked at this last.
Closing this as it is now superseded by #8551
This is being worked on as part of #8924

review_comments: `ioutil.ReadFile()` will already return the filename so `errors.Wrap(err, "unable to read token file")` is probably enough
